hook.text: Arabic and Hebrew are written without most vowels—'bk' could be 'book,' 'bike,' or 'bake.'

buildup.text: An abjad writes only consonants; readers supply the vowels from context and word knowledge.

discovery.text: This works because Semitic languages build words from consonant roots—vowels mark grammar patterns.

twist.text: Vowel marks exist in both scripts but are optional—used mainly for children and sacred texts.

climax.text: Abjads are efficient for Semitic languages because consonant roots carry the core meaning.

punchline.text: Skip the vowels and the meaning still comes through.
